articles.title: Ryanair brutally mocks Argentina after World Cup winner Rodri spotted on ultra-low-budget flight
articles.summary: Football News: Ryanair joins the football banter after Rodri, the World Cup-winning midfielder, is spotted on a budget flight, provoking a cheeky response aimed at Argentina.
articles.body: Ryanair has joined the growing social-media frenzy around Rodri's unlikely journey home, turning the Manchester City midfielder's viral economy-flight appearance into an opportunity for some football banter. After the Spain international was photographed boarding one of its flights from Madrid to Liverpool, the airline aimed its latest joke at Argentina with a pointed message about who qualifies as a “winner”.Ryanair gets involved in the Rodri frenzyThe viral moment began when Rodri was spotted waiting to board a Ryanair flight, wearing a baseball cap and sunglasses in an apparent attempt to keep a low profile.His personalised suitcase, carrying his name, Spain's flag and his squad number, quickly gave him away, and photographs of the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner travelling on a budget airline spread across social media.Ryanair wasted little time joining the conversation.The airline's official social-media account tagged the Argentina national team and posted the line: “We only fly winners.”The remark was a deliberately cheeky reference to Rodri's recent international success with Spain and the rivalry between the two football nations.The joke was aimed at Argentina's recent misfortunesRodri's journey had already attracted attention because of the contrast between his status and his choice of transport. The 30-year-old is one of the most decorated midfielders in the game, yet he was photographed standing in an ordinary airport queue rather than travelling privately.Ryanair's response shifted the story from admiration for Rodri's low-key approach towards football banter.The post quickly generated significant engagement online, with hundreds of thousands of interactions reported within hours as supporters reacted to the airline's attempt to turn a viral photograph into a piece of topical marketing.For Rodri, the attention comes after a remarkable summer with Spain. He was part of the World Cup-winning side and received the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, adding another major individual honour to the Ballon d'Or he won in 2024.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why referees are banned from speaking on TV at Real Madrid’s stadium despite La Liga’s new transparency protocol
articles.summary: Football News: Discover why Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu is the only La Liga stadium where referees cannot speak on TV, despite the new transparency protocol introduced by La Liga to improve communication with fans.
articles.body: La Liga has introduced a new refereeing protocol designed to give supporters more insight into how key decisions are made, with officials now able to speak on television about important incidents. But there is one notable exception to the new system: Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu.Referees will be able to give pre-match and post-match interviews at La Liga stadiums when requested by broadcasters, as well as explain the most significant decisions and incidents from games. The Bernabéu is the only one of La Liga’s 20 stadiums where the protocol cannot be used, because Real Madrid’s restrictions on broadcasters’ connections prevent the interviews from taking place. At every other venue, referees will be available to speak before and after matches.What is La Liga's new refereeing protocol?The policy marks a significant change from the traditional approach of referees remaining largely silent when it comes to explaining their decisions.The first referee interventions were heard during the opening round of La Liga, while the system is due to expand from Matchday 10. From that point, referees will be able to speak before and after matches when broadcasters request interviews, and they can also be asked about the most notable incidents from the game.The Spanish refereeing body has stressed that officials will speak in stadiums “where the necessary conditions for this are available”, while insisting there is no distinction between clubs or grounds.That means the intention is for supporters around Spain to hear referees explain some of the decisions that can otherwise leave fans debating what happened and why.Why is the Bernabéu the exception?The Santiago Bernabéu is the only La Liga stadium excluded from the new system, according to Catalan newspaper Sport.The reason is not that the refereeing committee has specifically banned Real Madrid from participating, nor is there a separate rule targeting the club. Instead, it comes down to the broadcasting arrangements at the stadium.Real Madrid restricts broadcasters' connections from the Bernabéu, allowing them to be established only a few minutes before kick-off. Those restrictions prevent broadcasters from creating the connections needed for the referee interviews to take place under the new protocol.In practical terms, referees can speak at other stadiums because the necessary broadcast infrastructure and connections can be arranged. At the Bernabéu, the existing restrictions make that impossible.A problem rooted in Real Madrid's tense relationship with La LigaThe broadcasting restrictions come against the backdrop of an already strained relationship between Real Madrid and both La Liga and the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF).That tension has also affected the conditions under which broadcasters operate from the Bernabéu. Real Madrid, under president Florentino Pérez, maintains restrictions on when broadcasters can establish their connections from the stadium, and those conditions now have a direct impact on the new refereeing transparency initiative.The refereeing body has made clear that this is not a decision by its officials to exclude Real Madrid. Its position is that referees will speak wherever the required conditions exist and that there is no discrimination between clubs or stadiums.What will fans see elsewhere?From Matchday 10 onwards, supporters at other La Liga grounds will be able to hear referees speak before and after matches when broadcasters request their participation. Officials will also be able to explain the most important decisions and incidents from the game.The measure is intended to provide greater transparency around refereeing decisions and give supporters a better understanding of why officials reached particular conclusions.The Bernabéu, however, will remain outside that system.So while the rest of La Liga moves towards giving fans more direct access to referees and their explanations, Real Madrid's home supporters will not have the same opportunity at their own stadium — not because referees have been instructed to stay silent there, but because of the broadcasting restrictions already in place at the Bernabéu.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dupla sertaneja viraliza ao fazer show vazio em aniversário de cidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentação de Sócrates e Matheus ocorreu com entrada gratuita no Parque de Exposições da cidade. Artistas afirmam que quantidade de público não altera entrega no palco.
articles.summary: Sócrates e Matheus viralizaram após show para 15 pessoas no aniversário de Naviraí, em Mato Grosso do Sul, mantendo a energia e o compromisso com o público presente.
articles.body:
A dupla sertaneja Sócrates e Matheus se apresentou para um público de ao menos 15 pessoas durante a festa de 63 anos de Naviraí (MS). O show ocorreu na noite de quinta-feira (12), no Parque de Exposições da cidade, com entrada gratuita. Veja o vídeo acima.

O registro em vídeo da apresentação mostra o contraste entre a estrutura do palco e o espaço praticamente sem espectadores. O registro viralizou nas redes sociais e reúne mais de 200 mil visualizações em apenas uma conta no Instagram.

A gravação foi feita pela estudante de direito Franciele Martins, que acompanhava a programação de aniversário do município. As imagens mostram os músicos mantendo o ritmo do repertório e interagindo com os poucos moradores espalhados pela arena.

A estudante Franciele Martins conta que parou para assistir ao espetáculo após notar a semelhança vocal dos cantores com a dupla Conrado e Aleksandro. Ao observar que os artistas mantinham o ritmo mesmo sem público na arena, decidiu filmar o momento para divulgar o trabalho dos músicos.

Para Franciele, a baixa adesão ocorreu pela preferência dos moradores por nomes de projeção nacional, já que a apresentação da cantora Mariana Fagundes, realizada na noite seguinte, reuniu público suficiente para lotar o estacionamento do parque.

"A minha opinião é que a cidade perdeu a oportunidade de curtir o show com desculpas de que era dia de semana ou que houve pouca divulgação, mas no dia seguinte estava lotado e todo mundo tinha que trabalhar do mesmo jeito. Dão preferência para cantores conhecidos e não dão oportunidade para os cantores locais"

A dupla Sócrates e Matheus se apresentou para um pequeno público em Naviraí. — Foto: Franciele Martins

Naturais de Mato Grosso do Sul e com 6 anos de carreira, os cantores afirmam que encararam a situação com naturalidade e entendem o episódio como parte da trajetória profissional. Ao g1 , Sócrates e Matheus explicaram que o número de pessoas na plateia não interfere na dedicação ou na qualidade do espetáculo.

Segundo os músicos, o compromisso no palco permanece o mesmo diante de dezenas ou de milhares de espectadores, com foco em transmitir emoção por meio das canções para quem decidiu acompanhar a apresentação.

"Subimos ao palco com a mesma energia, dedicação e verdade, independentemente de estarmos diante de 50, 5 mil ou 10 mil pessoas. O nosso compromisso é sempre entregar o melhor, com simplicidade, levando nossa música e transmitindo aquilo que ela tem de mais bonito: a emoção", afirmam os artistas.

Sócrates e Matheus. — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

A apresentação de Sócrates e Matheus abriu a agenda musical do rodeio "Cowboy de Aço 2026", etapa da Liga Profissional de Rodeio (LPR) realizada em comemoração aos 63 anos de Naviraí.

Além do show na quinta-feira (12), o calendário festivo no Parque de Exposições contou com apresentações de Mariana Fagundes na sexta-feira (13) e da dupla Vítor e Matheus no sábado (14), acompanhadas pela Prova dos Três Tambores, montarias em touros e atrações na Tenda Universitária.

*Estagiária sob supervisão de José Câmara.

Show da dupla Sócrates e Matheus com poucas pessoas. — Foto: Franciele Martins

articles.title: Neymar, se entrega al póker: termina décimo un torneo con 1,6 millones de reales en juego
articles.summary: Neymar, futbolista del Santos, se entregó a un fin de semana de póker en el que participó en una mesa con inscripción de 4.000 euros y otra de 8.000 euros en el 50K Super High Roller Invitational, en el que sólo participan personas invitadas.
articles.body: Neymar, futbolista del Santos, se entregó a un fin de semana de póker en el que participó en una mesa con inscripción de 4.000 euros y otra de 8.000 euros en el 50K Super High Roller Invitational, en el que sólo participan personas invitadas. El campeonato tiene lugar en el WTC Sheraton, un hotel de lujo en Sao Paulo (Brasil), y tiene un premio premio para el ganador de 1,6 millones de reales (256.320 euros) para el ganador. El sistema de competición es sencillo: todos los participantes se dividen en mesas y se enfrentan entre sí de forma aleatoria. La competencia se va reduciendo, y gana quien queda al final con todas las fichas. Neymar terminó en el décimo puesto entre 152 jugadores.

articles.title: Vinicius explica su bajón y habla de la renovación: “Me sentí realmente abrumado”
articles.standfirst: El delantero pide margen para Endrick y Estevão y reivindica el papel de Carlo Ancelotti en su carrera tras el doblete ante Japón con Brasil
articles.summary: El delantero pide margen para Endrick y Estevão y reivindica el papel de Carlo Ancelotti en su carrera tras el doblete ante Japón con Brasil
articles.body: Vinicius, que hizo dos goles en la derrota de Brasil ante Japón este sábado, admite que estuvo por debajo de lo que esperaba de sí mismo en los momentos decisivos. Con la Copa América en el horizonte, el delantero de Brasil tiene claro quién debe dar un paso al frente. “La mayor responsabilidad me corresponde a mí porque tengo más experiencia, porque soy uno de los mejores del mundo”, afirmó en rueda de prensa. “Creo que no me preparé mejor después del Mundial porque el impacto de este torneo es muy significativo para todos los brasileños. Perder tan pronto fue algo que no esperábamos. Así que aproveché las vacaciones para disfrutar, descansar, relajarme y pasar más tiempo con mi familia. Terminé entrenando menos que en los últimos años”, comentó Vini. Y añadió: “Esto puede haber afectado mi inicio de temporada. Además, con respecto a la renovación de mi contrato, con tantos clubes interesados el verano pasado, me sentí realmente abrumado, al igual que la situación en el Real Madrid. Pero la temporada es muy larga". Vinicius quiere que Endrick y Estevao tengan tiempo para crecer con la selección. El peso del equipo, a su juicio, debe recaer sobre él y los demás jugadores con experiencia. Entre ellos citó a Raphinha, Marquinhos, Gabriel Magalhães y Bruno Guimarães. El brasileño también recordó lo que supuso Carlo Ancelotti para él. “Cambió mi historia en el Real Madrid y en el fútbol”, dijo del entrenador que ahora le dirige en la selección. Vinicius contó que se alegró al enterarse de que el italiano iba a hacerse cargo de Brasil. Con los dos goles ante Japón, ya suma diez con Ancelotti al frente de la ‘canarinha’. El último gol de Vinicius con el Madrid se remonta al 26 de agosto de 2026, en el 4-1 ante la Real Sociedad. Aquella noche también dio una asistencia. Desde entonces han pasado 80 días y diez partidos suyos con el club blanco sin volver a marcar. Su balance, según Transfermarkt, es de un gol y tres asistencias en 12 partidos y 882 minutos entre Liga y Champions. Toda su producción ofensiva se concentra en el campeonato liguero. En Europa ha jugado cuatro encuentros sin marcar ni asistir. La sanción le dejó fuera de los últimos cuatro partidos de Liga, incluido el Clásico. Su última aparición con el Madrid fue el 4 de noviembre ante el AEK de Atenas, en Champions. Diez días después, con Ancelotti en el banquillo de Brasil, marcó en una tarde el doble de goles que lleva con el club blanco en toda la temporada.

articles.title: Aberdeen: What's at the top of Mario Frick's to-do list?
articles.summary: Mario Frick is Aberdeen's new head coach, but what does the former Liechtenstein striker have to do to lift his side clear of the relegation zone?
articles.body:
Mario Frick arrives at Aberdeen with the Pittodrie side sitting second bottom of the table and a game against relegation rivals Kilmarnock first up.

Lose that match and they fall to the foot of the Scottish Premiership. No pressure.

Apart from the obvious, what is it that the new head coach has to do to restore Aberdeen to previous glory days and avoid becoming yet another managerial failure at Pittodrie?

Okay, maybe this was obvious. But it's Aberdeen's clearest weakness this season.

They have the joint worst attacking record in the league, having only scored 12 goals and routinely looked completely short of confidence in front of goal.

Kevin Nisbet, the club captain, has 14 goals for the season. Nine of those came in the run to the Premier Sports Cup semi-final. Behind him, no-one has more than two.

Most concerning of all is that the Dons' have created the lowest xG (15.3) in the league so far. Not only are they not creating very many quality chances, they're struggling to take them.

They have just 3.3 shots on target per match, with a shot conversion rate of just 7.3%. Both metrics are the worst in the league.

Only Falkirk have created fewer big chances (19 to Aberdeen's 22) - the difference being John McGlynn's side score them.

One of the most frequent accusations that came predecessor Stephen Robinson's way was that his team lacked an identity and players looked unsure as to the tactical plan they had been told to carry out.

Given the Northern Irishman's clear style of play with St Mirren, that was a surprise.

His team in Paisley were known for their physically-domineering displays that were full of grit and graft. That wasn't the case in the North East.

Frick seemingly prefers a 4-4-2 formation, with the midfield playing in a diamond.

That might be bad news for new signings Tony Yogane and Lewis Smith, wingers who did get a look in under Robinson but struggled to make much of an impact.

Sticking to a consistent midfield will help with that. While Robinson regularly relied on Afeez Aremu in the middle of the park, the head coach often chopped and changed his midfield partner.

Of all of Aberdeen's 15 summer signings, Connor Ronan was the one that probably caused the most optimism. Another former St Mirren man, he impressed in his time in Paisley.

The Irishman won a move to Major League Soccer with Colorado Rapids off the back of that form and was also called up to the Republic of Ireland squad without winning a cap.

Eight goals from midfield in the 2021-22 season was a good return - and a couple of them were screamers.

Former Aberdeen midfielder Jamie McGrath recently reminded his old fanbase that they could do with replacing him after he scored a rocket for Hibs in the 4-0 win that did for Robinson.

Ronan could be the answer, playing in a similar role with the same attacking capabilities.

He has yet to hit the heights at Pittodrie, but if Frick can make him tick, the 28-year-old could fire Aberdeen back up the league table.

articles.title: El Madrid desactiva la alerta por Bernardo Silva
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista estará disponible para el regreso del equipo a la competición
articles.summary: El centrocampista estará disponible para el regreso del equipo a la competición
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha desactivado la alarma con Bernardo Silva y todo queda en un susto. El centrocampista abandonó la concentración de Portugal por precaución tras sentir unas ligeras molestias que finalmente no revisten ningún tipo de gravedad. De esta manera, Bernardo no está lesionado y estará disponible para Mourinho en el regreso del Madrid a la competición, el próximo sábado ante el Celta en el Bernabéu. Bernardo Silva había generado preocupación después de que la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) comunicase que había acabado con molestias el encuentro frente a Dinamarca y que, por ese motivo, no estaría disponible para el partido contra Gales. El jugador fue liberado de la concentración, pero lo hizo por precaución y el Madrid respira aliviado tras saber que no está lesionado. “Bernardo Silva fue evaluado clínicamente y declarado no apto por la Dirección de Salud y Rendimiento de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol”, fue el comunicado emitido por la Federación lusa. Ahora el jugador ya está de vuelta y se le espera para el sábado. El Madrid regresa este martes a los entrenamientos y será el momento de ir recuperando a poco a poco a los internacionales e ir evaluando a cada uno de ellos. El otro sobresalto durante el parón de selecciones lo protagonizó Tchouaméni. El centrocampista, que regresaba a la lista con Francia, se tuvo que volver a las primeras de cambio tras sufrir una lesión en el aductor derecho de la que lleva recuperándose desde el pasado 10 de noviembre. En su caso se irá viendo a lo largo de la semana su evolución y se tomará una decisión, sin arriesgar lo más mínimo y dando absoluta prioridad a su recuperación total antes de volver a estar a las órdenes de Mourinho. Asencio y Rodrygo son los otros dos lesionados, ambos de larga duración, y para su regreso habrá que esperar más tiempo.

articles.title: 'It's been a wonderful ride': Belgium's highest goalscorer Romelu Lukaku retires from international duty at 33
articles.summary: Romelu Lukaku announces retirement from international football, leaving behind a legacy as Belgium's all-time top scorer with 94 goals. His contributions to Belgium's golden generation include four World Cups and three European Championships.
articles.body: Romelu Lukaku has brought his Belgium career to an end at 33, retiring from international football as the country’s most prolific goalscorer and one of the defining players of its most successful modern generation. The Fenerbahçe striker leaves with 94 goals in 135 appearances, having represented the national team at four World Cups and three European Championships, including Belgium’s third-place finish in 2018.Romelu Lukaku retires with 94 goals in 135 appearances for BelgiumLukaku announced his decision on Monday through his official Instagram account, ending an international career that began 16 years ago. His 94 goals make him Belgium’s all-time leading scorer, well clear of Kevin De Bruyne, who is second on the list with 41.He also finishes fifth on the all-time list of men's international goalscorers, having established a record that places him among the most prolific forwards in the history of international football.In his message, Lukaku reflected on the emotional range of representing Belgium and thanked the players and coaches who had accompanied him throughout his career.“These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. I went through every emotion possible,” Lukaku said on Instagram.“I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for. I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team. It was a nice ride, and I enjoyed every single moment.”He also addressed Belgian supporters directly, expressing pride in the number of major international tournaments he had experienced.“To the Belgian fans, thank you for your continued support for our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships, and I will never forget these moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here.In a further message reflecting on his decision, Lukaku said: “I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing; it was enjoyable. I’m grateful - thank you.”A defining figure in Belgium’s golden generationLukaku’s international career coincided with Belgium’s emergence as one of Europe’s strongest national teams. He was part of the side that finished third at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, the country’s best result at the tournament, and went on to represent Belgium at four World Cups and three European Championships.His goalscoring record was a central part of that period. With 94 goals, he finishes 53 ahead of De Bruyne, the second-highest scorer in Belgium’s history. His 135 appearances also reflect the longevity of his involvement across successive generations of the national team.Lukaku began his professional career at Anderlecht before moving to Chelsea. His club career subsequently took him to West Bromwich Albion, Everton, Manchester United, Inter Milan, Roma and Napoli, with spells in the Premier League and Serie A establishing him as one of the most recognisable Belgian forwards of his generation. He currently plays for Turkish club Fenerbahçe.His international retirement comes after a difficult period with the national team. Lukaku was an unused substitute in Belgium’s 4-1 Nations League result against Italy on Sunday, despite completing lengthy warm-ups on the touchline. He had also been ruled out of the squad for the meeting with Turkey because of injury.The Italy match was therefore his final involvement in a Belgium squad, although he did not take the field. By the following day, he had confirmed that his international career was over.Lukaku’s departure leaves Belgium without the forward who has led their goalscoring charts for years. His retirement also gives the national team a significant decision to make as it looks to develop its next attacking generation, with no player currently close to matching his international record.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vinicius Jr: Real Madrid forward says transfer interest has affected form
articles.summary: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer.
articles.body:
Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season.

The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season.

He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real.

The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup.

"I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said.

"Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years.

"That may have affected my start to the season.

"On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season."

Vinicius received a red card for violent conduct in October when he pulled the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba, which led to a four-match suspension.

In his absence, record signing Yan Diomande has made the most of his opportunity on the left wing, scoring four goals.

Vinicius joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and has scored more than 20 club goals in each of his past five seasons.

Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, three points behind rivals Barcelona, and return to league action when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday.

articles.title: College Football Playoff projections: Here's what the picture looks like after a Week 11 devoid of upsets
articles.summary: The 12 teams in our first set of projections are the 12 teams in our second set of projections.
articles.body:
Our projected College Football Playoff field did not get shaken up on Saturday.

Sure, teams like Kentucky, LSU and South Carolina all lost, but we didn't think any of those three were ultimately making the postseason. Every team in our initial post-Week 10 projections won in Week 11.

But while the 12 teams in the field stay the same, we do wonder about some movement within the seeding. Here's our second round of CFP projections.

No. 1 Georgia (9-1, projected SEC champion)

The Bulldogs hardly had to sweat against Missouri on Saturday. LB Raylen Wilson intercepted Missouri QB Austin Simmons on the first play of the game and before anybody realized it, Georgia was up 21-0.

Georgia can lock up a spot in the SEC title game in Week 12 with a win at South Carolina. The Gamecocks will likely drop to the bottom of the CFP top 25 on Tuesday after they lost at Arkansas without QB LaNorris Sellers. We assume that Sellers will be able to go against Georgia.

No. 2 Utah (10-0, projected Big 12 champion)

If you stayed up late to watch Utah's win over Arizona, the Utes and Wildcats didn't bore you. Utah got a 40-39 win thanks to a 70-yard catch-and-run TD by Creed Whittemore late in the fourth quarter. Arizona had the chance for a game-winning field goal, but their fourth-down pass just before the two-minute warning fell incomplete.

The Utes travel to TCU in Week 12 as the Horned Frogs need to get a win over Utah or Texas Tech in the final two games of the season to make a bowl game.

The Fighting Irish had no problem with Boston College in a 41-7 win on Saturday. But we're wondering if Notre Dame's seeding will be impacted by another blowout that they had no part in. As Wake Forest demolished SMU — more on that game in a bit — the Mustangs now have three losses. And they're going to be significant underdogs and will likely get a fourth in Week 12 in South Bend. It's not Notre Dame's fault that many of the teams on their schedule have underachieved, but the Irish's second-best win is over a 6-4 Wisconsin team that lost to Maryland on Saturday.

No. 4 Indiana (9-1, projected Big Ten champion)

We were surprised the Hoosiers fell five spots on their Week 10 bye week but ultimately have no concerns about their chances of getting a first-round bye. If Indiana wins its final two games of the season and then the Big Ten title, they're in the top four. Period.

The Hoosiers also scored their most points since Oct. 3 in their 27-13 win over USC. That's not the mark of an offensive juggernaut, but Indiana doesn't have to be with a defense as good as it has. After QB Grant Wilson started against the Trojans, we wouldn't be surprised to see him take over for the rest of the season.

No. 5 Miami (9-1, projected ACC champion) vs. No. 12 Boise State (9-1, projected Pac-12 champion)

The Hurricanes had little trouble with Duke as they pulled away in the second half. Boise State, meanwhile, won a 46-41 shootout with Oregon State to wrap up a spot in the Pac-12 title game.

The Broncos are now the prohibitive favorites to make the College Football Playoff from the Group of Six conferences after New Mexico lost at home to UNLV. The Lobos now have two losses and it's hard to see how they have any playoff hopes barring a late-season collapse from Boise State.

Darian Mensah was 30-of-41 passing for 382 yards and a TD in Miami's 36-25 victory over his old school as Cooper Barkate — also a Duke transfer — had eight catches for 134 yards.

No. 6 UCLA (10-0, at-large) vs. No. 11 Tennessee (8-2, at-large)

Another week, another win for the Bruins. UCLA took down Illinois 22-14 on Friday night despite an injury scare from Ty Dieffenbach. Remember, he's been starting at QB for Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava's season-ending knee injury. In this potential matchup, Iamaleava would be watching from the sidelines this game between his current and former schools.

The Volunteers dominated a Texas A&M team that is just offensively hapless. But with LSU dropping out of the rankings and Vanderbilt also in the cellar of the SEC, their final three games aren't going to be seen as a gauntlet by the committee. If Wake Forest and Texas Tech keep piling up the points, the Vols could end up the last team in the field at 10-2.

No. 7 Alabama (8-2, at-large) vs. No. 10 Wake Forest (9-1, at-large)

Again, this is a ranking predicated on Alabama losing the SEC title game to Georgia. We don't think the committee would put a one-loss UCLA behind a three-loss Alabama, but we also wouldn't rule it out, either.

Keelon Russell threw three TDs in the Tide's win over Vanderbilt on Saturday as Alabama overcame a sluggish first half.

There was no sluggish first half in Dallas for Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons absolutely blitzed SMU 49-7. Wake had a 42-0 lead at halftime and five different players rushed for a touchdown. Ty Clark III had 11 carries for 77 yards and a score, QB Gio Lopez rushed for two TDs and threw for another and breakout wide receiver Carlos Hernandez had six catches for 94 yards and a score.

No. 8 Texas (8-2, at-large) vs. No. 9 Texas Tech (9-1, at-large)

This would be a fantastic first-round game. The Red Raiders seem to have found something offensively with Thomas Castellanos at quarterback. Tech beat Oklahoma State 52-27 Saturday night and has now scored 139 points across his three starts. Saturday night, Castellanos was 12-of-23 passing for 263 yards and four touchdowns while also rushing for 38 yards before leaving the game early after a big hit.

Arch Manning produced the signature drive of his Texas career as the Longhorns knocked LSU out of CFP contention. It was a great rebound for Manning after what had been a brutal game. It was the first three-interception game of his career, as he finished 19-of-35 passing for 174 yards.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Stock Report: Drake Maye injury clouds outlook for entire Patriots offense going into Week 11
articles.summary: Matt Okada takes you through his biggest risers and fallers coming out of Week 10 for fantasy football.
articles.body:
As I was writing this on Sunday night, 13 of 14 Week 10 games were in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the fantasy season is now past the halfway point. Still, things are changing every week. Promising improvements. Concerning trends. Performances that change our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy.

With that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 11.

It's been an excellent month-and-a-half for Blake Corum, but Week 10 felt like the true takeover in Los Angeles. He totaled 119 yards and a touchdown on 20 touches — logging his sixth straight game with a touchdown — while Kyren Williams managed just 32 yards on 14 touches. (And Ronnie Rivers vultured an absurd 15 carries for 81 yards on a single clock-killing final drive.) Since Week 5, Corum's 14.8 fantasy points per game rank 11th among running backs and he's hit 11+ fantasy points in every single game (bolstered by those touchdowns). With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out for the foreseeable future, the Rams will rely heavily on the run game and Corum has steadily shifted to the forefront of that run game. He's now a borderline must-start running back and could be a huge playoff asset after L.A.'s Week 11 bye.

Immediately following the Week 6 "Benchgate" with Skattebo, there was fear that he would be a fantasy bust with a confusing role over the second half of the season. Yeah, not so much. In his two games since, he's shouldered 35 carries and four catches for 243 total yards, three touchdowns and 44.3 fantasy points. He's seen at least 15 touches in every single game outside of the unofficial benching, and has looked more explosive and punishing as a runner and a receiver these last couple of games. Best of all, after scoring just one touchdown through the first six weeks, he's now scored three over these last two games. He has an awful matchup with the Jaguars next week — which could make him a trade target heading into Week 12 — but should be a high-floor, high-end RB2 moving forward.

I was honestly baffled by how available Jordyn Tyson was on waivers heading into Week 10. He will not be available after Tuesday evening. The highly-drafted rookie caught 11 of 13 targets on Sunday, for 80 yards, and still wasn't playing the full share of snaps in his second game. And it wasn't like this breakout came in the absence of Chris Olave — the veteran played the entire game and ran nine more routes, but caught just three of four targets for 30 yards. Tyson has now seen a target on a wild 37% of his routes through two games and caught 82% of those targets. I wouldn't say he's leapfrogged Olave as the WR1, by any means, but he was the eighth overall pick for a reason. He still has more ceiling to discover as he ramps up to a full snap share and the Saints don't have a bottom-10 wide receiver matchup left on the schedule. Don't be surprised if he's an intermittent WR2/3 the rest of the way.

Oddly enough, Zach Charbonnet's return from injury has not looked great for fantasy — three straight games with single-digit fantasy points in half-PPR looks middling at best. But the usage, the tape and the metrics have been excellent. Over the last two weeks, Charbonnet has handled 36 carries for 171 rushing yards (4.8 per carry), with 101 yards after contact . He hasn't found the end zone or been particularly involved as a receiver, which has severely capped his fantasy ceiling, but this kind of ground-game usage can lay the groundwork for RB1 upside once the scores come. Remember, this is the guy who scored 12 rushing touchdowns last year, with Kenneth Walker III on the roster, so we know he has the skill set to do it. He has a Week 11 bye to continue working his way back to 100% — assuming he's not there already — and has great matchups with the Cowboys and Panthers left on the schedule. Expect Charbonnet to be a bell-cow back in a strong run-first offense down the stretch ... an excellent recipe for fantasy success.

George Pickens is the last name in this Stock Up section for a reason. His 38.0 fantasy points on Sunday were incredible. He caught 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and a TD hat trick. He did it against a 49ers defense that had been stingy to wide receivers all season and has two far juicier matchups with the Titans and Eagles on deck (and in the hole). But, With all that being said, my takeaway from Week 10 is not that Pickens is now back to what he was in 2025, or that he'll be a consistent WR1 or even WR2 the rest of the way. Instead, my takeaway is that Pickens does still have his rare week-winning upside and that he can play as the WR1 when Dallas needs him to. Considering this was his best game of the year in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns, there's no doubt it's an encouraging performance and that his stock is UP on the whole. Just know that he'll probably have several more single-digit fantasy days mixed in with his 20- and 30-burgers.

While we're still waiting on an official diagnosis or prognosis, reports are that Drake Maye could have a fractured ankle and miss significant time , if not the rest of the season. For now, he's considered out indefinitely. The Patriots offense had already been a little up-and-down with Maye, but for as long as it's Tommy DeVito at the helm, things are going to be messy. And Maye is honestly just the tip of the iceberg. New England's offensive line has been ravaged by injury, A.J. Brown cannot stay healthy for a single game, the running backs are battling a variety of health issues and this offense is running through guys like Mack Hollins and Lan Larison (don't even bother looking him up; it's just that bad). Hunter Henry couldn't manage a decent stream in a dream matchup, Corey Kiner did nothing with the lead-back role and DeMario Douglas disappeared after earning all sorts of sleeper hype following a strong month. Until further notice — or unless the news on Maye changes dramatically — I would aim to avoid this offense whenever and wherever possible.

I truly didn't think this was possible. Easily fantasy's most consistent tight end, arguably one of its most consistent players at any position, Trey McBride had been an unwavering star through the first two months of the season. But with the departure of Jacoby Brissett and the debut start for Carson Beck, McBride recorded season lows in targets (five), catches (five) and fantasy points (6.2), while narrowly avoiding his season low in yards (31) with 37 on Sunday. For what it's worth, the Rams are a very tough defense for tight ends, whereas the Chiefs and Commanders — his next two matchups — have been extremely friendly. And he gets the Saints and Raiders in the fantasy playoffs. So we're not panicking or knee-jerk trading here. In fact, with Brock Bowers getting banged up in Week 10, McBride might have a tighter hold on the TE1 spot now than he did entering the weekend. But it's also likely that his floor and ceiling in fantasy will be slightly lowered with Beck under center.

I hate to be the bearer of bad news, especially on promising, young players. But that's sort of what this section of this column is all about. And I have very bad news on Jalen Coker: He's droppable. After a monster game in Week 1 against the Bears, Coker has flashed a time or two briefly ... but he's ultimately averaged 5.1 fantasy points per game since, has not scored 13+ points once and has just logged his fourth straight game in single digits.

Sunday was particularly discouraging, as he caught zero of his four targets against the Saints for a fantasy goose egg. Wide receivers with more fantasy points than Coker since Week 2 include Rashod Bateman, Malachi Fields, Jaylin Noel and Romeo Doubs (in just five games). Carolina's passing attack is sputtering in general, and Coker's tank is completely out of gas. Unless you have an incredibly deep bench, you can send him to the waiver wire for more intriguing youngsters like Caleb Douglas or Antonio Williams.

After holding Jonathan Taylor through the trade deadline — despite shipping off basically everyone else of note — the Colts proceeded to split his workload with Seth McGowan ... and give the rookie the goal-line rushing touchdown. Taylor still managed 83 yards on 16 carries and 20 yards on two catches, but McGowan racked up 77 rushing yards of his own (on 6.4 per carry) and scored Indy's only rushing score. In previous weeks, this would have been 20-25 touches, over 100 yards and a score for Taylor. And keep in mind, this was a rare win for the Colts (barely), thanks to the fact that they were playing the Dolphins with a backup quarterback. A quick glance at the schedule does not offer much hope for Indianapolis, which means game scripts could get messier for Taylor moving forward. This is his third straight game with fewer than 12 fantasy points, and it's beginning to look like his time as an every-week RB1 in Indy has come to a close.

Wan'Dale Robinson was already more of a sleeper than a trustworthy starter from week-to-week, but Sunday's game put the nail in his fantasy coffin. With Carnell Tate out and Cam Ward throwing 39 passes for 231 yards ... Robinson caught three balls for 10 yards and 2.5 fantasy points. Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, Xavier Restrepo, Gunnar Helm and Tony Pollard were all more productive as receivers, and even backup tight end Daniel Bellinger outscored him in fantasy with a two-yard touchdown. Tate will return and Robinson has yet to crest 13 fantasy points, with or without the rookie WR1, since Week 3. He's a full drop, even in deeper PPR leagues, where he's been more of a trap than a contributor in fantasy.

articles.title: ACC suspends Louisville's Stanquan Clark and UNC's Greg Smith III for a half after post-game brawl
articles.summary: After the final kneel down, Louisville and UNC went at it Saturday.
articles.body:
Louisville's Stanquan Clark and North Carolina's Greg Smith III won't be available during the first half of their team's respective games Saturday. Both players were suspended for one half by the ACC on Monday.

Clark and Smith were suspended following a post-game brawl after Louisville's 16-14 win over UNC on Saturday.

In addition to those suspensions, both Louisville and UNC were fined.

Per the ACC's statement, the actions of both players "violated the ACC Sportsmanship Policy." The conference called the behavior of both Clark and Smith "unacceptable."

The brawl occurred following the final kneel down by Louisville with 14 seconds to play. Before time ran out, a few players on both teams started shoving each other. That led to an all-out brawl involving multiple players on both sides. It's unclear exactly what Smith and Clark did to earn their suspensions.

In the broadcast video, Smith can be seen early in the clip getting into it with Naeer Jackson of Louisville. Whatever happened between the pair moved away from the broadcast view, though may have resulted in players running to the end zone during the brawl.

Clark wasn't on the field initially and it is hard to find him amid all the chaos.

As a result of their actions, Smith will miss the first half of Saturday's game against Virginia and Clark will miss the first half vs. Pittsburgh.

The suspensions are significant for both teams. Clark leads Louisville with 74 combined tackles. He's also registered seven sacks. Smith leads UNC with three interceptions and ranks third on the team with 56 combined tackles.

articles.title: UEFA backs French football chief Philippe Diallo to challenge Gianni Infantino for FIFA presidency
articles.summary: French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo will challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in March 2027 after securing the
articles.body: French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo will challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in March 2027 after securing the backing of UEFA, setting the stage for a contest over the leadership and governance of world football's governing body.UEFA announced on Monday that its member associations represented on the executive committee and the FIFA Council had unanimously pledged their support for Diallo to stand against Infantino, who is seeking a fourth term as FIFA president. The election is scheduled to take place in Rabat, Morocco, on March 18, 2027."At a meeting held today and chaired by UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the UEFA Executive Committee and the FIFA Council invited Philippe Diallo, President of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support," a UEFA statement said.Diallo has accepted the invitation, with his candidacy due to be formally ratified by the FFF Executive Committee at its meeting on Tuesday.The development comes amid growing opposition to Infantino following his aborted proposal in July to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions, including the World Cup. The initiative triggered concerns over transparency and governance among several European associations, with the French federation among those withdrawing support for Infantino's re-election.UEFA flags concerns over FIFA's directionUEFA said its member associations wanted a change in the way the global governing body operates, calling for greater unity, trust and accountability within the football community."Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community," UEFA said."They also called for a FIFA that places the development of the game in every region of the world at the heart of its mission, upholds the highest standards of governance and works in close partnership with its member associations, confederations and football stakeholders."They expressed their full confidence in Philippe Diallo to provide the leadership needed to achieve this ambition."The UEFA executive committee met on Monday to settle on a candidate ahead of Wednesday's deadline for nominations. Diallo's emergence follows discussions within the European body over finding an alternative to Infantino, who is seeking another term after becoming FIFA president in 2016.The FFF had already distanced itself from the incumbent in September, withdrawing its support for his re-election. Diallo had made his position clear at the time, saying: "the trust placed in the FIFA president has been broken".He had also indicated that European associations needed to put forward an alternative capable of contesting the election."We will need to be ready by then to put forward a candidacy capable of winning the FIFA presidency," Diallo said in September.Who is Philippe Diallo?The 63-year-old has been at the helm of French football since 2023. He was initially appointed interim FFF president in January that year following the resignation of Noel Le Graet, before being elected five months later to serve until the end of 2024. He was re-elected in December 2024 for a four-year term.Diallo joined the FFF in 2021 and became its vice-president later that year.Infantino, meanwhile, is preparing to seek a fourth term when FIFA's member associations vote in March. The Swiss-Italian administrator has faced criticism over the proposed commercial entity, which was eventually abandoned following opposition from football stakeholders.Diallo is not the only figure to have expressed an intention to challenge Infantino. Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima announced his intention to run earlier in November, while former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his plans last month.Candidates require the backing of at least five national associations to stand in the election. With UEFA now throwing its weight behind Diallo, the contest for FIFA's top post has entered a new phase.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Otra joya de Valdebebas se cae del Mundial sub 17
articles.standfirst: El canterano Gorka Abascal es desconvocado por Colombia por lesión
articles.summary: El canterano Gorka Abascal es desconvocado por Colombia por lesión
articles.body: Otra joya de Valdebebas se pierde el Mundial sub 17 por lesión. Una semana después de que Enzo Alves fuese baja con la selección española, ahora ha sido Gorka Abascal el que se queda fuera de la de Colombia, también por problemas físicos. El propio combinado colombiano ha hecho oficial la decisión. "El cuerpo técnico de la Selección de Colombia comunica que el jugador Gorka Abascal presentó una lesión en el último partido con su club, Real Madrid, la cual le impide sumarse a la convocatoria que participará en la Copa Mundial Sub-17 de la FIFA Catar 2026. De acuerdo con el parte médico, el futbolista presenta una lesión muscular de grado II del músculo oblicuo interno derecho. El entrenador, su cuerpo técnico y el grupo de jugadores le desean a Gorka una pronta recuperación", reza el comunicado. Gorka Abascal, en plantilla del Juvenil B, se lesionó el pasado 7 de noviembre en el último partido con el Madrid antes de incorporarse a la selección colombiana para preparar la cita mundialista. El centrocampista, de sólo 16 años, iba a estar presente en la cita de Qatar en su condición de una de las grandes promesas de La Fábrica. El jugador, que durante los últimos tiempos ha ido alternando su presencia con las selecciones de España y de Colombia, por su doble nacionalidad, había apostado por la segunda en las últimas semanas, después de que ya participase con Colombia en un reciente torneo UEFA sub 18 previo al Mundial. Tras la baja de última hora de Gorka Abascal, son cinco los madridistas que estarán presentes en el Mundial sub 17: Guille Ponce, Company y Yeremaiah (España), Lemaitre (Francia) y Edu Corlat (Rumanía).

articles.title: Afcon 2027 qualifying: Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on spots at finals
articles.summary: Cameroon, Senegal and Benin are on the brink of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, while Ghana secure another crucial win in their bid to reach the finals.
articles.body:
Nicolas Jackson was on target again as Senegal, Cameroon and Benin moved to the brink of qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with away victories.

After Aston Villa striker Jackson had opened the scoring, Senegal gave up a 2-0 lead against Sudan before two late goals sealed a 4-2 win, while five-time Afcon winners Cameroon cruised to a 3-0 triumph over Namibia.

A goal in second-half stoppage time from Ede Oloko sealed a 1-0 success for Benin against Central African Republic.

All three sides are on 10 points in their respective groups after four rounds of matches and will progress to next year's finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda if other results go their way on Tuesday.

Elsewhere, Jordan Ayew's first-half penalty was enough for Ghana to register back-to-back victories over Somalia in Group C.

The Black Stars had home advantage for what should have been an away tie, with the game played in Sekondi-Takoradi because the Ocean Stars do not have a stadium fit for international football.

Ayew had a penalty saved as Ghana beat Somalia 2-0 in the reverse fixture last Thursday, but the Sheffield United forward kept his composure when he sent the goalkeeper the wrong way in the 36th minute after Brandon Thomas-Asante had been pulled down in the box.

Ghana, who parted company with Carlos Queiroz after losing their opening two fixtures, move level in the table with The Gambia, with both sides on six points.

Salah scores twice as Egypt and Nigeria win Afcon 2027 qualifiers

Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

The Gambians are themselves three points adrift of group leaders Ivory Coast before they host the Elephants on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Guinea moved to the top of Group D after Yakhouba Barry scored twice in their 3-1 away win over Eritrea in neutral Cairo.

The West Africans lead South Africa, who travel to Kenya on Tuesday, by two points in a group with only one qualification spot available because the Kenyans are assured of a spot at the finals as co-hosts.

And Zimbabwe beat Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare to go two points behind Group E table toppers DR Congo.

Thando Ngwenya, Tawanda Chirewa and Tawanda Maswanhise were all on target for the Warriors before Equatorial Guinea's Josete Miranda had a penalty saved and Saul Coco was sent off for the visitors late on.

The National Thunder were without first choice goalkeeper Jesus Owono after he asked not to be selected following his involvement in a collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died the day after the incident.

DR Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali and Morocco can all book their tickets to the tournament when the fourth round of fixtures culminates with 18 matches on Tuesday.

The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in East Africa from 19 June to 17 July.

Patrick Vieira's Senegal survived a scare in neutral Juba after Jackson's early goal put the Teranga Lions ahead and a low strike from Brentford left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf made it 2-0 midway through the first half.

Sudan hit back through Al-Gozoli Nooh and Salah Adel to level proceedings with 15 minutes to play, but Pathe Mboup's lob made it 3-2 in the 87th minute and Paul Mendy made the points safe for the West Africans in the first minute of added time.

Senegal are still awaiting the outcome of their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over the destination of the 2025 Afcon title.

The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 after extra time in January's final, but a Confederation of African Football appeals board stripped them of the title two months later, decreeing Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.

Mahamadou Nagida opened the scoring for Cameroon against Namibia in neutral Botswana with a stunning volley from outside the box in the 12th minute, and Ryan Fosso's deflected effort doubled the lead just before the hour mark.

Saidou Alioum made it 3-0 with a fine first-time volley with 19 minutes remaining, and David Pagou's men will be assured of a place at Afcon 2027 if Congo-Brazzaville fail to beat Comoros on Tuesday.

Zimbabwe 3-0 Equatorial Guinea (Group E)

Central African Republic 0-1 Benin (Group F)

articles.title: Jude Bellingham card worth £150,000 rejected on the spot: Collector keeps ultra-rare piece with special message inscribed by star himself
articles.summary: A collector turned down a £150,000 offer for a unique Jude Bellingham trading card with a special inscription, highlighting the surge in the football memorabilia market. Discover the significance behind this one-of-a-kind piece.
articles.body: A £150,000 (approx.$198,000) offer would be enough to make most collectors think twice, but one owner was not prepared to part with a rare Jude Bellingham trading card at that price. The story left former Manchester United and England goalkeeper Ben Foster astonished when it came up during a discussion about the growing football memorabilia market.Ben Foster stunned by rejected £150,000 offerFoster heard about the remarkable deal while discussing his experience at the London Card Show on his podcast, the Fozcast. The former goalkeeper, who has since built a media career through his YouTube channel and podcast, has also entered the trading card market himself, having acquired a one-of-one Rio Ngumoha card.Describing the scale of the collecting scene, Foster spoke about seeing a Rio Ngumoha one-of-one booklet change hands for £14,000. The card had been pulled during a Whatnot break, and another collector offered the owner the money after seeing its Liverpool patch and unique design.But it was a story involving Bellingham that really caught his attention. Foster's co-host, Tubes, explained that a collector had been offered £150,000 for one of the Real Madrid midfielder's cards."The London Card Show was incredible. Honestly," Foster said.He went on to describe the collections on display, some reportedly worth around £250,000, before Tubes revealed the Bellingham offer."A guy walks up, he's like - '£150,000 for that card'. Liam went no.""Wow," Foster replied.Tubes clarified that £150,000 was the opening offer, but the owner was not interested in selling.What makes Jude Bellingham's card so rare?The card is a 2023/24 Topps Stadium Club Chrome UEFA Champions League Marks of Excellence Black Foil autograph, one of one. Its defining feature is a handwritten inscription by Bellingham: "Brum to the Bernabéu".The message captures the midfielder's journey from Birmingham City to Real Madrid, making the card particularly meaningful to supporters who have followed his rise. Its one-of-one status also means there is no identical copy elsewhere.According to Tubes, the owner has a strong personal connection to Bellingham, Birmingham and the player's collection, which explains why he was unwilling to accept the offer. He is also a Birmingham City supporter and owns several other Bellingham cards.The card has even been photographed at St Andrew's, Birmingham City's home ground, reflecting the connection behind the inscription.Football trading cards are attracting extraordinary sumsThe rejected offer is another example of how much collectors are prepared to pay for rare football memorabilia, particularly cards featuring established stars and emerging talents.Foster's account of the London Card Show included the £14,000 sale of the Ngumoha card, while the wider market has seen some of the most sought-after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo cards reach seven-figure valuations. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has also been associated with a card valued at around £1 million.Topps and Panini have helped expand the market, with specialist collectors' events and flagship stores in cities including London and Paris drawing greater attention to the hobby.For Bellingham's owner, however, the decision appears to go beyond the potential resale value. The inscription links the card to the player's journey and Birmingham roots, and £150,000 was not enough to persuade him to let it go.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Dios silbe a la reina'... otra vez
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: Sonaron los primeros compases del 'God save the queen' y buena parte del público se puso a silbar. Uno que hace ruido siempre vale por diez que se callan, pero en todo caso no se trataba de un sector precisamente minoritario. Superado ese tramo de vergüenza la pelota echó a rodar... y del himno inglés se pasó a la sinfonía inglesa. Notablemente superiores en el juego, los 'Three Lions' también pusieron distancia en el marcador. Cayó uno, cayó otro, cayó un tercero y último. El arreón final español, eso sí, dejó en resultado mínimo lo que apuntaba a goleada. 2-3. Era partido oficial, por cierto. De la Nations League... Y no, el párrafo anterior no se refiere a los sucesos del domingo en el Metropolitano. Porque la historia se repite y porque el hincha es el único animal capaz de tropezar en la misma piedra tantas veces como resulte necesario. Aquello sucedió el 15 de octubre de 2018, hace poco más de ocho años. En el Benito Villamarín, entonces. Y con un tal Harry Kane presente, único entre los que visten de corto que ha tenido la fortuna (o la desgracia) de repetir... Así, que como uno se va haciendo viejo y como ciertos comportamientos son tan previsibles, resulta que ya estaba escrita la columna sobre los defensores de la patria que envueltos en banderas hacen con el himno de los demás lo que no les gusta que se haga con el suyo. Porque también se hace, claro: en las finales de Copa, sin ir más lejos. Y la nueva versión de tanta falta de respeto pasa por esos cánticos sobre botes en los que incluso participan futbolistas de selecciones autonómicas. Parece que, definitivamente, tiene mucho más sentido negar la identidad ajena que afirmar la propia. Del 'Dios salve a la reina' al 'Dios silbe a la reina'. Así nos va...

articles.title: UConn men’s basketball moves up to No. 3 in AP Top 25
articles.summary: The Huskies are up one spot after two wins last week.
articles.body:
UConn men's basketball moved up one spot in this week's poll to No. 3 after convincing wins over Wagner and Ohio State last week. The 4-0 Huskies are behind just No. 1 Florida and No. 2 Michigan State in the polls. Over at KenPom, UConn is ranked No. 8 overall, with the 17th-best offense and seventh-best defense in the country.

Despite losing Duke transfer Nik Khamenia to a foot injury in last Monday's win over Wagner, the Huskies navigated some first-half foul trouble to cruise to a win over an unranked but tough Ohio State team . This week, UConn has only one game on its schedule, but it's a big one, as the Huskies head west to take on No. 12 Arizona on the road in a top-15 matchup.

Arizona stayed at No. 12 for the second-straight week, but is still a top-10 team nationally according to KenPom. Duke, which UConn faces in Las Vegas on Nov. 23, fell three spots to No. 5 after losing to Michigan State in the Champions Classic last week.

Future opponent Virginia rose to No. 4 this week, while Illinois dropped seven spots to No. 10. Kansas jumped four spots to No. 11. While all five of those upcoming matchups figure to be tough without Khamenia, help may soon be on the way as Solo Ball was cleared for full-contact practice with the team as of today.

St. John's remains the only other ranked Big East team in the polls, with the Johnnies ranked at No. 13. Xavier was the only other school in the conference to receive votes.

articles.title: Manchester United have set their sights on move for Premier League defender
articles.summary: Manchester United weigh Calvin Bassey transfer as January plans take shapeManchester United are seriously considering a move for Calvin Bassey as Mauricio Po...
articles.body:
Manchester United weigh Calvin Bassey transfer as January plans take shape

Manchester United are seriously considering a move for Calvin Bassey as Mauricio Pochettino and the club hierarchy shape their defensive plans for January, with TeamTalk reporting that the Fulham defender is seen internally as a strong tactical fit.

The interest is understood to pre-date Pochettino's appointment at Old Trafford, which is significant. Recruitment work had already been undertaken on Bassey, and the arrival of the Argentine has only strengthened that position. The key detail from the report is that the Nigeria international is regarded as a "very good fit" for the new head coach's system.

Calvin Bassey seen as strong tactical fit

That phrase matters. Pochettino's sides have long been associated with an aggressive defensive line, mobility across the back line and the ability to recover quickly in transition. In that context, Bassey's athletic profile stands out. He is quick, physically dominant and comfortable defending larger spaces, attributes that are increasingly non-negotiable for elite teams trying to play on the front foot.

There is also a practical element to United's thinking. Bassey can operate as a left-sided centre-back and at left-back, which gives the club what the report describes as a "double reason" to consider a deal. That versatility inevitably sharpens the focus on the wider balance of the squad, particularly given the uncertainty around Luke Shaw's contract situation.

Sources cited in the report state Bassey is viewed internally as a "very good fit" and, crucially, that he "would be more than open to the prospect of a move to Old Trafford". For any club planning a major January move, alignment on profile and player willingness is a major starting point.

Fulham contract stance could shape January window

United's interest does not automatically make this straightforward. Fulham retain a degree of control over the situation. Bassey is approaching the final months of his deal, but the west London club hold an option to extend. The report states they have already indicated an intention to trigger that option if fresh contract terms cannot be agreed.

Even so, the position appears far from fully settled. Alvaro Arbeloa is said to want Bassey to stay, yet talks over an extension "have not progressed as hoped". That has left his camp attentive to developments, with outside interest beginning to build.

It is in that context that United are prepared to explore whether Fulham's stance can be tested in the January market. Clubs do not move aggressively in winter without conviction, and this is a case where the tactical argument and the market opportunity may be converging.

Manchester United face £40m-plus Calvin Bassey valuation

The obvious complication is price. TeamTalk reports that a fee "in excess of £40million" would likely be required, with Fulham potentially seeking close to £50million before considering a sale. That is a substantial figure for a January deal and would represent a major decision for United, particularly with other areas of the squad also requiring attention.

For Fulham, a sale at that level would carry historic significance, surpassing the £43.5million received from Al-Hilal for Aleksandar Mitrovic in 2023. That context helps explain why they are under no pressure to soften their position quickly.

United are understood to want a new left-sided central defender regardless of any eventual call on Lisandro Martinez, whose future remains open according to the report. Bassey is one of several names under assessment, alongside Jarrad Branthwaite, Nathan Collins and Castello Lukeba, but there is a sense that his combination of suitability, versatility and openness to the move has elevated him within the process.

If this report is accurate, the logic is easy to follow. The biggest appeal with Bassey is that he seems to answer more than one question at once. Manchester United need speed in defence, more security in wide areas and better protection against transitions. A player comfortable at left centre-back and left-back immediately improves the options available.

The valuation is the sticking point. Paying more than £40m in January for a defender who is highly rated but not yet universally viewed among the very top bracket feels like a serious gamble. Fulham would be well within their rights to demand it, especially with his physical tools and Premier League experience, but United have been here before with expensive deals that made sense on paper and looked far less convincing later on.

Still, there is something encouraging about the profile. This sounds like a move driven by system fit rather than reputation. That is how recruitment should look. If Pochettino wants defenders who can hold a high line and recover fast, then Bassey ticks obvious boxes. The mention that he is "more than open to the prospect of a move to Old Trafford" also suggests this would not require selling a dream to a reluctant target.

The concern is whether United can get this done at the right number. If the fee moves towards £50m, alternatives such as Branthwaite or Lukeba may start to look more attractive. Even so, Bassey feels like one to watch because the need, the style and the player profile all appear aligned.

articles.title: New France international gives credit to one man for his incredible success
articles.summary: Senny Mayulu is a real talent and seems like a lovely kid. He’s been speaking about making his France debut this week.If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want...
articles.body:
Senny Mayulu is a real talent and seems like a lovely kid. He's been speaking about making his France debut this week.

If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Senny Mayulu has been the star of this international break, from a PSG point of view.

He was starting regularly for the Parisians before the break, and continued that run with a first call up for France's senior team, then a debut for Les Bleus against Italy this week.

But Mayulu was clear on who the credit should really go to: Luis Enrique.

Mayulu credits coach for impressive start to senior career

Senny Mayulu. (Photo by Catherine Steenkeste/Getty Images for Qatar Airways)

"He's my first coach, he helped me enormously to make the leap from youth player to professional. He helped me progress and he still does so every day in Ligue 1," Mayulu said in quotes picked up by FootMercato.

"I'm finding it hard to believe, it all happened so fast. It was my first season as a pro, and we immediately won the Champions League. We did it again the following year. After that, you get a taste for it and you want to win it all the time. A third Champions League title? The coach keeps us hungry for more, despite having already won the two. We're still working every day towards it."

Fabian Ruiz finished tenth in the Ballon d'Or and thinks he should have done even better, given his accomplishments this year.

Senior PSG officials are using this international break as a chance to get contract talks going with several key players.

France are back in action on Sunday, and ahead of the game Zinezine Zidane has been praising Desire Doue.

articles.title: Hungary boss confirms Dominik Szoboszlai fitness as Liverpool prepare for Manchester United
articles.summary: Hungary manager Marco Rossi has addressed Dominik Szoboszlai's fitness ahead of Liverpool's highly anticipated Premier League game against Manchester United...
articles.body:
Hungary manager Marco Rossi has confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai is healthy and not dealing with any injury concerns.

Szoboszlai was substituted during Liverpool's 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace prior to the international break. The Reds midfielder sustained a minor knee issue during the triumph at Selhurst Park, requiring heavy strapping to make it to the 69th minute, yet still traveled for international duty with Hungary.

Concerns resurfaced, however, ahead of Hungary's game against Georgia on Saturday. Szoboszlai featured and registered an assist in the 2-0 victory in Tbilisi, but admitted post-match that he had contemplated withdrawing during the warm-up.

"I came today with a workout and a half in my legs," he said via The Mirror . "During the warm-up I was close to saying no, because I felt my leg on one of the shots. But if I've come this far, I won't let the team down. I went as best I could, trying to give my best."

Szoboszlai remains a pivotal figure for Liverpool, who welcome Manchester United to Anfield on Sunday following the international break. Reds boss Andoni Iraola will be anxious to have his influential midfielder return unharmed after Hungary's last UEFA Nations League group stage fixture against Northern Ireland in Budapest on Tuesday.

Hungary manager Rossi remains adamant that Szoboszlai is fully fit. "Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?" he said in his pre-match press conference on Monday. "I didn't see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

"I don't think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don't think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Tension has emerged between Hungary and Liverpool regarding Szoboszlai, with Iraola making his position clear that he wanted the 26-year-old to sit out this round of Nations League fixtures due to the knee issue.

"The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games. Last time, we lost three very important players," he said. "It's the last thing we need, so I hope he can take care of it. I think he extended a little bit the knee, he was fine, but not 100 percent.

"So he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not, but also hope that it doesn't happen like the other international break when we lost Alex [Alexander Isak], Cody [Gakpo], Dom. So, touch wood, we are in a better place in two weeks."

Across all competitions for Liverpool this season, Szoboszlai has registered three goals and one assist in 11 appearances.

articles.title: UVA basketball climbs to No. 4 in latest AP Poll
articles.summary: The ’Hoos enter the top four after their comeback win at Maryland.
articles.body:
The Virginia Cavaliers (5-0, 0-0 ACC), fresh off their come-from-behind four-point win over Maryland on Friday evening, rose two spots to No. 4 in this week's AP Poll, released Monday afternoon.

At No. 4, the 'Hoos have now entered the AP Poll's top five for the first time since appearing at No. 2 on December 12, 2022, which marked the fourth and final week that UVA was inside the top five during the 2022-23 season.

Monday's ascension in the polls comes after Virginia overcame an 11-point halftime deficit inside the Xfinity Center on Friday evening against former ACC rival Maryland. In what was the 186 th edition of the all-time series against the Terrapins, Sam Lewis erupted for a career-high 28 points as the 'Hoos shot 76.9% from the floor in the second half to storm back and silence a sold-out Maryland crowd.

The win in College Park completed a 2-0 week for Ryan Odom's squad after Virginia bested Bucknell, 95-61, at home inside John Paul Jones Arena on Tuesday night.

Aside from the 'Hoos, the ACC suffered a rough week in the rankings. Former No. 2 Duke dropped three spots to No. 5 following a loss to Michigan State in Tuesday night's Champions Classic, while former No. 10 Louisville plummeted 13 spots to No. 23 after a 20-point road loss at Memphis. No. 17 Miami, the conference's only other ranked team, stood pat after a pair of buy-game wins.

At the top of the rankings, No. 1 Florida held on to the top spot after a nine-point road win over in-state rival Florida State on Tuesday; No. 2 Michigan State jumped up three spots after taking down the Blue Devils; and No. 3 UConn climbed one spot to round out the top three.

The fourth-ranked 'Hoos, who enter the week at No. 6 in Bart Torvik's T-Rankings and No. 12 at KenPom, will return home for a pair of weeknight matchups inside JPJ with Old Dominion (Tuesday at 9 PM) and Loyola MD (Friday at 7 PM).
